visuals.title: The deal
visuals.name: Blackstone / Hilton Hotels
visuals.sub: An all-cash buyout of the hotel group, months before the financial crisis
lines: $47.50 a share, 32% above that day's close; about $26bn including debt

visuals.at: Hilton went public again on the twelfth of December
visuals.title: Hilton: eleven years in and out
rows: Debt restructured: $800m of new equity, debt cut to $16bn
Back on the stock market, raising about $2.35bn
A quarter of the company sold to HNA Group for $6.5bn
visuals.note: Blackstone sold in stages from 2014. Result: about $14bn of profit, more than three times its money.

visuals.at: The multiple of money, M-O-I-C, says how much
visuals.title: The money multiple
visuals.formula: MOIC = total cash returned ÷ total cash invested
visuals.note: How much came back for every pound put in. It says nothing about how long that took: that's the IRR.

visuals.at: Check it: four hundred, then four hundred and eighty
visuals.title: Harbour: 400 compounding at 20% a year
visuals.note: Sofia's 30% a year (150% ÷ 5) ignores compounding: at 30%, 400 becomes nearly 1,500.

visuals.at: The full definition: the discount rate
visuals.title: The internal rate of return
visuals.note: The discount rate at which the net present value of all the fund's cash flows, in and out, is zero. With one cheque in and one out: IRR = MOIC^(1 ÷ years) − 1.

visuals.at: About thirty-six percent a year. Over five years
visuals.title: Same 2.5x, different holds: IRR
visuals.note: Same multiple, same £600m of profit on £400m. The IRR falls by more than half.

visuals.at: Suppose all the money had come back in one go
visuals.title: Three times the money: IRR by holding period

items.label: 3x over 11 years, all back at the end

visuals.note: A simplification of Hilton: in fact Blackstone's money came back in stages from 2014, so its real IRR was higher than the first bar.

visuals.at: It made fifty. Harbour made six hundred
visuals.title: A quick flip against Harbour
visuals.note: A short hold flatters the IRR; a long hold flatters the multiple. Investors look at both.

visuals.at: Third trap. The new debt comes off the exit price
visuals.title: A dividend recap: same multiple, higher IRR
visuals.note: The £200m dividend is borrowed by Harbour, so it comes off the exit. Extra interest ignored to keep it simple.

visuals.at: Double your money in three years
visuals.title: IRR shortcuts to learn
visuals.note: Rule of 72: 72 ÷ the annual rate ≈ the years it takes to double.

visuals.title: Leverage and returns

items.label: rise in Mobico's equity value if its enterprise value rises 10% and the debt doesn't change

visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: A fund puts in 400 and takes out 1,000 five years later. Roughly what is the IRR?
questions.explain: 400 compounding at 20% a year reaches about 1,000 in five years. Dividing the 150% gain by five gives 30%, which forgets compounding.
questions.explain_at: The I-R-R is the yearly rate that turns four hundred into one thousand

questions.q: A fund doubles its money in five years. Roughly what is the IRR?
questions.explain: 1.15 compounded for five years is about 2. Sofia's 20% (100% ÷ 5) would compound to about 2.5x; 26% is doubling in three years.

questions.q: Two years in, Harbour pays the fund a dividend funded with new debt, and the total cash back is unchanged. What happens?

options.text: The extra dividend lifts the multiple and the IRR
The multiple rises; the IRR is unchanged
The IRR rises; the multiple is unchanged

questions.explain: The new debt comes off the exit, so total cash, and the multiple, stay the same. Cash arriving three years earlier lifts the IRR, from about 20% to just over 24%.
questions.explain_at: Early cash lifts the I-R-R and leaves the multiple where it was

questions.q: Blackstone more than tripled its money on Hilton. Why is its IRR well below what 3x in five years would give?

options.text: The profit was small for a deal that size
The money was at work for about eleven years
The debt restructuring cut most of the gain
A multiple above three overstates the profit

questions.explain: The same multiple spread over more years means a lower annual return: 3x over 11 years is about 10.5% a year if all paid at the end, against about 25% over five.
questions.explain_at: Suppose all the money had come back in one go

questions.q: Mobico's equity is worth about £308m and its enterprise value about £2.3bn. If the enterprise value rises 10% and the debt doesn't change, roughly how much does the equity rise?
questions.explain: 10% of £2.3bn is about £230m, and all of it goes to £308m of equity: a rise of about 75%. Sofia's 10% forgets the debt in between.
questions.explain_at: On three hundred and eight million of equity, that's a rise of about seventy-five percent
